title: Creating Your First Project 🎮
description: Choose a template and create a new project.

slides.title: Project Browser 🗂️
slides.content:
# Starting Fresh

When you launch Unreal Engine, the **Project Browser** appears. Here you can:

* Create a **New Project** from a template
* Open an **existing project**
* Browse **samples** from the marketplace

We’ll create a new project from a template – perfect for learning.

slides.title: Templates Explained 🧱
slides.content:
## Choose Your Starting Point

Templates give you pre‑made assets and logic so you don’t start empty.

* **Blank** – empty world, no rules
* **First Person** – character with camera, movement, and shooting
* **Third Person** – character with third‑person camera
* **Top Down** – click‑to‑move gameplay
* **Vehicle** – drivable car

For this course, pick **Blank** to learn from scratch, or **Third Person** if you prefer a character.

quizData.question: Which template should you choose to start completely empty?
quizData.explanation: The Blank template gives an empty world with no pre‑made logic, ideal for learning fundamentals.

slides.title: Project Settings ⚙️
slides.content:
## Customize Your Project

After selecting template, configure:

* **Blueprint or C++** – Choose **Blueprint** (no coding needed)
* **Maximum Quality** – Default (can change later)
* **Raytracing** – Keep disabled unless powerful GPU
* **Starter Content** – Check this! It gives free basic assets
* **Project Name & Location** – Name it `MyFirstProject`

Click **Create** and let the magic happen!

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Starter Content is Gold

Always enable **Starter Content** – it adds basic materials, shapes, and props that you can use immediately. Without it, you’ll have to create everything from scratch!
